newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore zoo kills escaped tiger.
newsitem.headline: Singapore zoo kills escaped tiger.

text.p: Singapore zookeepers shot dead an escaped tiger that was just a high-jump away from the freedom of a nearby forest, the New Paper said on Wednesday.

The paper quoted zoo boss Bernard Harrison as saying Giggo, a hand-raised, 14-month-old Malaysian tiger got into a pen of African cattle and was chasing them around -- out of the range of a tranquilizer gun.

He said keepers became worried when Giggo started eyeing a 2,000-acre (810 ha) forest on the other side of the 2.1 metre (6 ft 8 in) fence, where it would have been difficult to recapture him. They then decided to kill the tiger.
Harrison said the zoo had no idea how Giggo got out.
"We checked the enclosure and nothing was damaged. All the doors were locked, fences untouched. Nothing was broken either," he was quoted as saying.
